analysis.title: US CPI in Focus, Riksbank Screens Hawkish, BoC Minutes Later Today
key_insights: Fed Governor Waller said a core CPI reading of 0.3% or higher warrants a 50bps hike. Before last month's reading, the last core CPI print above 30bps was in April.
After Waller's comments the December Fed stub closed the gap and trades at about 25bps of hikes.

UBS Economics has core CPI in line with consensus, which has converged toward UBSe (26bps and 23bps for core vs. 27bps and 22bps). UBS nowcasting is slightly hotter on headline (+32bps) and cooler on core (+22bps).
The percentage of CPI items rising above a 2% rate has been in steady decline.

The BoC summary of deliberations is due later today, covering its first 25bps hike this year. The policy rate is 2.50%, in the lower part of the BoC's neutral range estimate of 2.25% to 3.25%, and the desk sees a move to the 2.75% midpoint as increasingly likely.
OIS implies about two BoC hikes over the next year, with the December and January meetings contributing to the first hike in roughly equal parts.
The Riksbank minutes read hawkish and the SWESTR curve is cheaper by about 5bps. The minutes say underlying inflation drivers point upward and the policy rate may need to be raised a few more times.
Largest daily moves adjusted for three-month realized volatility: USDNOK +1.2 std dev, EURNOK +1.4 std dev, SEK front end rates +1.3 std dev, USDTHB -1.3 std dev, USDPHP -1 std dev.
